text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link N300 WiFi Extender(TL-WA855RE)-WiFi Range Extender, up to 300Mbps speed, Wireless Signal Booster and Access Point, Single Band 2.4Ghz Only Short version: When used appropriately, this is a great device at a great price. Simple installation options and useful features. Stronger wireless transceivers than my Netgear cable modem/router. The key here is a lot if not most people don't know how or when to use these devices...so I'll try to help with that below.

Long version: Let's assume you're buying this for your home to extend existing WiFi coverage. Before you do anything, conduct an analysis of existing networks in your area and what frequencies and channels they are using. On 2.4GHz, channel 1, 6, and 11 do not overlap. Ideally, you want to be using one of these channels without anyone else nearby using it so go ahead and reconfigure your router to meet that criteria. There aren't any overlapping channels on 5GHz and it may be used less by your neighbors so that could be worth pursuing for you as well. Next, try moving your WiFi router around to find the ideal spot to cover the entire house. If your router has external antenna(s), you can try using a more directional antenna if you think that'll help and your router has connections for it or reorienting existing antennas. If you find a perfect configuration with this that works everywhere in the home, run a new cable to that location for your Internet if necessary and you're done and didn't need this device.

Now on to tips for setting up this device. Use a different SSID than your existing one by appending something like "_EXT". This will help you troubleshoot any issues in the future and help get you on the right network at the right times. Do upgrade the firmware on it after initial setup. Keep in mind, no affordable repeater seamlessly bounces you to whichever device has the best signal at any given second. That is handled by the client, i.e. your phone, laptop, etc. and it's not always perfect. I haven't tried it, but I think this device can be wired to your router. That is the best way to use this, but may not be required depending on your situation. If extending it using only WiFi, put it somewhere that has decent signal already and will reach to where you're lacking signal.

The Power schedule and LED on/off schedules are nice touches. It increased my coverage and bandwidth 5x where I needed it to after an easy 5-10 minute setup including getting the firmware and applying it. I am a former networking professional. I didn't go in to extreme detail because this is a review, not a blog...research anything I mentioned where you have questions and the info is out there. Or have a buddy help you with it or a company that does residential on-site work and don't let them bill you more than an hour and a trip charge.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link N300 WiFi Extender(TL-WA855RE)-WiFi Range Extender, up to 300Mbps speed, Wireless Signal Booster and Access Point, Single Band 2.4Ghz Only

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black Short story of the review is that these are just as they say they are--a pair of relatively inexpensive "basic" earphones. As such, they seem to be a decent value and have some good points, but if you're looking for sound quality over price, you'll want to go elsewhere.

Pros:
Packaging: small and minimalist as it should be

Provided with: multiple size earbuds caps and ear inserts (more on these later), a very short charging cable, and a decent zip-around traveling pouch

Pairing: No problem with any of my Apple devices. Instantly recognized and paired with an iPhone (8 and 6), iPad (Pro and Air 2), and MacBook Pro. Couldn't be quicker or easier each and every time

Comfort: This was an issue for me, though obviously this is a pretty subjective category. I had to step down immediately to the small caps/rings, which is no surprise--I do that with I think all of my earbuds. But even with the smalls I just couldn't get a a good seal or a comfortable, though oddly enough much worse with my right. The left was not "great" but was certainly good; right was a bad seal and wholly uncomfortable no matter what I tried. Weird.

Sound quality: Again, it's a matter of pricing here. I don't own many basics and it's been years since I've had a set of lower-tier earbuds, so it's hard for me to compare at an equal level. The sound is what I'd call adequate, especially for exercise or listening to an audiobook. But there's no comparison to my PowerBeats3 or Jaybird X2s, and not even to my Jabra Elites, which I"d call my mid-range ones. The first two are in a whole other class in terms of range, sharpness, richness, and comfort, while the Jabras are a good step up in both sound and comfort. Sound here is more than a little thin at both ends, and just not very rich or full. Less noticeable with an audiobook, but definitely not the buds I'd choose if I'm focusing on listening to music, as opposed to having background sound while I"m doing something else. Phone quality is pretty similar--adequate, at times a bit muddy.

Controls: easy, intuitive, and responsive

Overall, if you want a basic set where quality of sound isn't a deal breaker, or a pair of cheaper ones for places you might have to worry about forgetting them, these will suit the bill, assuming you don't have the same comfort issue I did. But for someone looking for rich, full sound, particularly for music, I'd strongly advise moving up the ladder
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black

text_fidelity_a: BlastCase 3 Pack of Premium Crystal Clear Screen Protectors for Apple iPad I was hesitant after reading the mixed reviews.  However these were at a price I just could not pass up.  Shipping took a little time, but I received the 3 pack as advertised.  The film is applied similar to other protective films, one just need to follow the steps to ensure a good application.  The most important things are to work clean and work fast!  You have to thoroughly clean the surface - I use some water and microfiber cloth.  There must be NO dust at all on the screen, use some canned air if you need.  Lay down the sticky film by carefully lining up the hole with the home button and make sure the bottom edge is level.  Then work efficiently and briskly at applying the film from bottom up.  When I applied I got a couple little bubbles; as long as they are just air bubbles you can always work them out to the edge.  If you got dust trapped in there, they will be more or less permanent bubbles.  Work cleanly and efficiently and you should have a nice invisible shield on your ipad in no time!
text_fidelity_b: BlastCase 3 Pack of Premium Crystal Clear Screen Protectors for Apple iPad

Canon PowerShot ELPH 520 HS 10.1 MP CMOS Digital Camera with 12x Ultra Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom Lens and Full 1080p HD Video (Blue) I'm really happy with this camera. It takes great snapshots, and it is so small that I can always have it with me. Nobody will ever mistake it for a several thousand dollar DSLR, either in price, weight, or picture quality, but the 12x zoom in such a small package was the sweet spot for me. And lets face it, for most of us, being able to get the shot because you have your camera is much more important than the really high quality picture--that you're never going to blow up to room size anyway--that you would have got if only you hadn't left your big, heavy, awkward DSLR at home!

Some folks have compared the quality to cell phones. There's no comparison. I can get shots that are just dark blobs on the iPhone. The battery is pretty small, though, so make sure you have two or three, which I have always done anyway (they're small, so it isn't that big a deal). Be careful if you buy an off brand battery: Many of them have LESS capacity. Don't go by the picture, many of them appear to be photoshopped to say 1000mAH, but the specs give you the real value. I picked up the [[ASIN:B004M640YU Wasabi Power Battery for Canon NB-9L and Canon PowerShot SD4500 IS, ELPH 510 HS, ELPH 520 HS, ELPH 530 HS]], and it seems OK so far, but I haven't rigorously tested it. The reviews were pretty good, though.

Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black The good:

Its slim profile. But it will still hold a lot of gear.

The case within the backpack that slides in and out the side hatch, with positionable dividers. Just right for GoPro or sports type cameras.

The laptop section. My laptop measures 10 by 15 inches and an inch thick. It fits like the pack was made for it. I doubt any larger laptop would fit. The laptop section is right on the back, but there is padding to keep things comfortable.

The shoulder straps are comfortable and very adjustable.

The designed places for headphones and small tripods/monopods and batteries and other various gear.

The expandable pocket on the side opposite the inner case hatch.

It has several straps to grab and carry the pack or stow extra items.

It's well made, with even stitching throughout.

The not-so-good:

The waist strap is a sufficient length. But the chest strap is way too short. A teenager would have trouble fastening it. That's a bit of a concern if you're bombing down a hill on a bike and only one of the two front straps is long enough to latch. It kind of compromises the security.

It's not versatile. It's a little too small for DSLRs or bridge cameras. If the slide-in case and backpack were just an inch or so deeper it would hold them. That's not really a flaw though since this was designed for GoPro or sports type cameras and gear.

I think there was a missed opportunity to put an expandable pocket or two on the front. The pockets there will only hold flat materials. But that does keep the profile neat and slim.

Overall it's a really good pack, but maybe could be a smidgen better.

It's far worse than the old TV it replaced and off-angle viewing is terrible. We also discovered that the audio is very weak. The TV was returned today. There are much better choices. We were roped in by the headphone jack but it's not worth it. Very poor TV.
.
Original Review - I bought this 24" Vizio because it was the only one in it's size that has a dedicated headphone jack. It connected to WI-fi without a problem and I signed into Netflix. I noticed right away that the opening screen was washed out and dull. I tried several different movies and shows and they all looked washed out. After 10 minutes of fiddling with all of the image controls, the image was improved but was still poor compared to our 10 year old LG in the other room. To save log-in time, I connected an already logged-in Roku to the HDMI input on the TV.
As soon as I selected the Roku HDMI input the on-screen image dramatically improved. Checking the same Netflix movies and shows as before, it was always much brighter and more vibrant than when using built-in streaming. Images on other services like Hulu were also quite watchable.
I was going to return the set until I hooked up the Roku. With the improved image coming from the HDMI input, my wife and I will give it a week's trial.
I would strongly not recommend this set if you intend to use its internal ("smart") capability. If you're going to use an external Roku, Chromcast, Apple TV, or similar HDMI-connected box, it's worth a try considering the price and inputs and outputs. The audio quality is adequate. Neither bad nor great.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO 32-inch D-Series Full HD 720p Smart TV with Apple AirPlay and Chromecast Built-in, Alexa Compatibility, D32h-J09, 2022 Model

I have Windows 10. Knew from reading through the Amazon product description that I should not use the CD that came with the product and should not download drivers from Broadcom.com. Plug the Kinivo USB adapter into my computer and Windows 10 automatically and quickly takes care of everything needed.

I had no problems getting my computer and LG cell phone to find each other and pair, but I kept getting "No Services Found" when I wanted to transfer photos from my phone to my computer. Kinivo customer support was very responsive, got back to me quickly with detailed instructions on various things to try. I did make some changes to settings and learned quite a bit about the product.

It turned out right clicking on the Bluetooth Device icon on the lower right on my computer screen (mine is in "hidden icons”) and selecting "Receive a File" was the final step needed. Now no problem transferring photos from my phone to my computer.

I was very impressed with how quickly customer support got back to me when I sent my first email. Took several emails but Brian was courteous and obviously wanted a satisfied customer. All that support comes with a product that only cost $9 with free shipping. Very happy with my purchase.

I am setting up an A/V system and these will now be rear speakers with a pair of Pioneer Floor standing up front.  I have a subwoofer behind my Entertainment Furniture as it sits out from a corner and has the room back there.  I have had these Pioneer SP-BS22-LR Andrew Jones Designed Bookshelf Loudspeakers set up as front speakers now for a month after breaking them in for about two days of music, all day long and they improved daily and then I moved them to the living room. Transcend 16GB SDHC Class 10 Flash Memory Card Up to 30MB/s (TS16GSDHC10) If you're buying this 32gb class 10 chip to operate in a Canon HFS100 solid state camcorder, forget it unless you want to record at XP+ (12mbps) or lower. The two higher quality bitrates MXP (24mbps) and FXP (17mbps) will not record. Very disappointing.

Also, when you select Memory Card Info from the menu, it does not recognize the card as Class 10. It says it's 32gb and displays all the other info, but not its class speed. The manual clearly states the HFS100 will record on Class 4 "or higher" SDHC cards. Except in the case of Transcend, it won't work. I really wanted to use this for long runs in my HFS100. The camera is clearly capable of handling 32GB cards, just not Transcend Class 10 32GB cards. According to Canon, there are no firmware updates announced for this camera. Bummer.

Fortunately, the card seems to work fine in the little GoPro Hero HD camcorder, so I guess that's where it will reside.

If you go to the Transcend website, they don't even list this part number. I'm sticking with better name brands for my cards.

text_fidelity_a:
Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer) I was able to do a direct side-by-side comparison between three Logitech webcams: the C920, C615, and C525. Here is what I found:

Right away I noticed that the C920 was a superior product - as it should be, considering it is Logitech's flagship webcam at the moment. But my initial impression was that the extra features might not be worth the size and setup tradeoff. There are three things that the C920 does not have:

1) While all three models attach to your computer monitor in about the same way and all three can tilt up and down, only the C525 and C615 can turn side to side. In fact, they can turn around 360 degrees and more. The C920, however, has a threaded tripod mount, as does the C615.

2) The C920 lacks the excellent "fold-and-go" design of the other two models, which makes packing and travelling easy, while protecting the lenses. In contrast, the C920 is much larger and stationary.

3) The C615 comes with a shorter USB cable AND an extension for more versatility. The C920 - like the C525 - comes with only a full length cable (~6'). My wish for all three models is that they come with a detachable USB cable, which would make them all much more portable and easy to carry around, especially in this age when most people travel with at least one or two USB cables.

But when I actually sat down to do some serious comparisons, I realized just how much more advanced the C920 is, most notably in its use of H.264 compression and its autofocus feature.

H.264 is a standard being utilized more and more for video of all sorts, and it makes a huge difference here. Having used all three webcams on the same computer and with the same software, the C920 compresses 1080p video completely while recording and takes about 49MB per 1 minute of recording on the highest settings (720p for one minute takes about 31MB). That uses *.mp4 format.

Meanwhile, the C615 and C525 use *.wmv format and take 99MB and 44MB for one minute of video at 1080p and 720p, respectively. The real problem, though, is that you then have to sit and wait for the video to compress if you are working in 1080.

If you're interested, The C920 has 1 zoom level at 1080 and 4 levels at 720. The C615 has 0 zoom levels at 1080 and about 10 at 720. The C525 has about 10 at 720. All can be used during recording, but the quality involved with the C920 is again far superior.

Also, the autofocus is much better on the C920, with less flickering and light change. You can really get up close and show off your pores and beard growth.

In conclusion, the optics and hardware of the C920 are obviously superior to the others, which are already high quality. If I am using the webcam while highly mobile, then I may opt for one of the others - I might even just settle for the C525 because it's a tiny bit smaller than the C615 and I believe you cannot use the C615 to make 1080p video calling, even if your hotel's Internet service could keep up with the data rate. However, if I am using a webcam at a stationary computer, or am really a videophile, then I definitely want the bigger workhorse.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Pro Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Pro

64G Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, Mp4/Story Player, Music Player, Supports FM Radio of High Volume Built-in Speaker, 4-Inch LCD Full Touch Screen, E-Book, Micro SD Card Slot Ups to 512GB (Black) It does what it's sold to do very well. I've tested several types of ebooks (PDFs, epub, doc, txt), mp3 files of various quality, pics, and vids (avi, x264, and x265) - it read and ran everything well and smoothly.
Basically it's a low-end phone running an old distro of Android. It's super locked down and there's no internet access, so there's no updating and no adding of apps - this includes bluetooth tethering. That being said, a few of the apps are ones I've used for ages and (obv) I like them: specifically moon reader, the ebook reader - it really works well on this device. And I believe the video player is MX Player, also an old fav. Moving files via TF card was a bit of a pain, as the older version of android only supports up to 4GB at a time, but otherwise it moved everything without error. I tested the reader with several cards, from a generic 32gb to a samsung 512gb u3, and they all read well, so you can easily have a large library of media at hand. There's no cam or wifi; and there aren't any sensors, so it can't tell tilt, ambient light, etc. The screen is tiny but looks surprisingly good. The speaker is decently loud, but it def sounds like a phone speaker, still though, it's better than expected.
If you just want a simple media device with some neat features (FM works really well btw), this is great. I both would and wouldn't recommend this for kids - you can't add any educational apps (or games, lol), and they wouldn't be able to access things like their school portal or wiki; but if you only want your kid to have books, vids, and audio with a few tools (calc, calendar, alarm), this is right up your ally. Heads up though, they can swap out the TF card if they have a media collection you don't know about, and Moon Reader supports requiring passwords for opening the app.
If you want something you can do more with, I'd suggest foregoing the 50% off coupon and getting a burner phone at this device's list price. A burner probably won't work as smoothly (because it will have more hardware/software), but it'll have wifi and an app store and updates.
I plan to use this as an extra/backup media device. I'm one of those weird people that has a TF collection in my bag with tons of movies, tv, games, etc. I'm going to put one of those pockets on the back for credit cards, and use a TF card organizing card to hold my cards, so I'll have all my media together and with a device that can play them, in case my phone is AWOL or dead. IMO, after the coupon, it's worth the price as long as you know what you're getting.
text_fidelity_b: 64G Mp3 Player with Bluetooth, Mp4/Story Player, Music Player, Supports FM Radio of High Volume Built-in Speaker, 4-Inch LCD Full Touch Screen, E-Book, Micro SD Card Slot Ups to 512GB (Black)

Sony WHXB900N Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset - Blue (Amazon Exclusive) Sony WH-XB900N Wireless Noise Canceling Extra Bass Headphones have great sound quality. Plus, for an over the ear headphone they are surprisingly lightweight. I also like how they bend to fold up and are really pliable. However, that's really where the greatness stops. Pairing these with any device I own is difficult or doesn't happen at all. These will not pair with my laptop. My laptop sees it's there. It claims it's playing from the headphones, but alas it does not most of the time. In addition, these will not play from iTunes. So, if you have an Apple device forget it. These will not pair with my iPhone 5. For two reasons, first, these are terrible with Apple devices/software and second, you must have the App to pair the headphones, which if you have an older phone won't happen because the App is only compatible with certain iOS systems. As much as I am angry with Apple for stopping all updates for older Apple devices (which work just fine otherwise), it's equally frustrating with App developers who do not design their Apps to be compatible with the older systems. So, most of my experience with these headphones is through the AUX jack.

Therefore, the sound quality is really good. I listen to a lot of hiphop and the bass is spot on. However, I do listen other types of music (pretty much everything) and I would have to say listening to Beethoven's 6th and Old Blind Dogs was a nice experience as well! The noise cancelling is a joke. I can hear everything around me still. In fact, I'm currently wearing these as I type this review and can hear the click clack of the keys, my son bump around upstairs, and my father just call my name. So, if you wear these on public transportation or at work, you're gonna hear everything as usual. But they are good headphones and comfortable on my ears.

The instructions are ridiculous. Can we stop with the picture instructions? They make no sense. I need words and should not have to depend on internet video reviews to get clarity on how to use anything. There is a way to play, pause, volume down/up by tapping or swiping, but I have no idea how to do it. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. They have a long battery life. I charged these weeks ago and they still have a charge as I use them now.

So, these have a great sound quality, the noise cancellation doesn't do anything, and you need to pair these with non-Apple devices.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black This is a fancier version of the popular Blue Yeti amateur-quality USB microphone with a much higher price tag ($170 vs $110). For the extra money, you get 4 condensers (instead of 3) to give you higher-resolution 24-bit audio (instead of 16-bit) plus a bunch of fancier control and display options. The new microphone has the same directional recording patterns to isolate the recording to your intended audio sources. Is the new microphone worth the extra money? If you really need 24-bit audio, then definitely yes. If not, the new display and control features are more convenient than a huge jump in functionality. The Blue Yeti is still a great microphone for amateur USB recording (podcasts, musical performances, etc). The new version is a step forward, but not worth the price for everyone.

My biggest complaint is that the new microphone uses the same ancient mini-USB interface as the old one. Modern ultralight laptops are moving to the USB-C standard and mini-USB is 2 generations old. You could use a USB-C hub to give you a mini-USB interface, but I wish all modern devices came with USB-C ports since this has been the standard for the last few years.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech for Creators Blue Yeti X Professional USB Condenser Microphone for PC, Mac,Gaming,Recording, Streaming, Podcasting on PC, Desktop Mic High-Res Metering, LED Lighting,Blue VO!CE Effects-Black

text_fidelity_a: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Earbuds Headphones, Earphones with Microphone and Nylon Cable (Turquoise Blue). I have always been a big skullcandy fan (I know, I probably just lost most people reading this review, but hear me out). I am a hipster when it comes to skullcandy, I was skullcandy back in 07-08 when they were actually of quality. No different than the first set of beats that were good, and everything recent is subpar. Now, I continued purchasing skullcandy because I was never good to my earbuds. The average lifespan of my earbuds was about 2 months, so the cheap quality was fine. But when I started med school and had to study all the time, I found my earbuds finally lasted over a year, but the quality was bugging me. They wouldn't cancel out the annoying undergrads who used the library for socialization rather than studying. I decided to finally to invest in pair of higher quality earbuds. I was willing to spend beats price if I was going to get quality. Little did I know there existed a pair of earbuds roughly equal in price to my skullcandy, but outclasses them when it comes to quality. All of my friends who have tried these earbuds have had to switch. They have a great sound, noise cancel, and have a mic if you're into that. The one negative (hence the minus 1 star) is that the jack has this "nub" that when pressed in my pocket pauses my music. This is very annoying for walking to class or the bus. But when I'm sitting and studying, I would choose no other.
text_fidelity_b: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Earbuds Headphones, Earphones with Microphone and Nylon Cable (Turquoise Blue).

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Home Speaker 300: Bluetooth Smart Speaker with Amazon Alexa Built-in, Silver This is a great speaker! It has great Bose sound and gets loud!!!!
The speaker is very well packaged. The cable has built in clips to keep it organized.
The speaker requires the Bose Music app.
There isn’t much instructions that come with the actual speaker - it’s all online.
The actual setup process took me about 20 minutes. It took me a few attempts to connect and I did need to unplug the device and wait about a minute once.
The touch pad is very responsive and the voice pickup is great!
I don’t have to yell at it like some of my other devices!
The presets are pretty easy to setup. I set them up using both Amazon Music and Pandora.
In the Alexa app the Bose speaker is found under the Echo & Alexa group. It’s currently not able to be added to a speaker group as it’s treated more like a speaker than an Alexa. Hopefully an app update will change to allow this.
I also have a Bose Revolve and was hoping to sync the two but this hasn’t been possible.
The Revolve used the Bose Connect app and not the Bose Music app. That was a little disappointing but nothing I really needed to do and doesn’t change the greatness of this speaker.
There is a port on the bottom of the speaker that I’m not sure what it’s for. It’s a standard plug but a cable didn’t come for it.
Overall this is a great speaker with great sound and Alexa works perfectly! The setup was pretty minimal and it’s easy to use.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Home Speaker 300: Bluetooth Smart Speaker with Amazon Alexa Built-in, Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White I'm sure they do it for shipping purposes and to appeal to homeowners without tools, but I don't like that they give you multiple short pieces instead of fewer long pieces that you could cut down to appropriate size. That just means you need more couplers; each additional coupler decreases the appeal of the final installation.

Honestly, I hate surface mounted conduit. But there are times when it is required, and in those cases better than nothing. I own my home, so of course I put all permanent links properly inside the walls, but even then, there are times when the Cat/RG/other jacks are not directly behind the furniture holding the devices that need the cables. In these cases, I prefer to mount these with screws, and then caulk and paint them into the painted baseboards so they blend in better, although they have made these with tape for truly temporary installations.

There is just one connector for an inside corner and an outside corner (on the x/z axis). And in my opinion, these are the only two you should really need, and you probably need more of them. I am never going vertical up walls with cables; I just go from the jack along the baseboard to behind the furniture...if I need more than that, I'm afraid I need to just stop being lazy and tear down a wall or something.

I get that if you are in an apartment or a rental property, you may need more flexibility with this. But in my opinion, if you can't do a proper wall-mount TV install without surface-mount conduit, then you should just use a TV stand as God intended because this is not enough to make cables acceptable in such an install (although honestly, it is better than nothing).
text_fidelity_b: Legrand - Wiremold Cable Management Kit, Cord Organizer and Hider, Concealer, C210S Cord Cover Kit, White

Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black) I live on a farm, so I spend a lot of time outside doing various things. I usually wear a pair of Skullcandy Hesh headphones, but I’m worried that constantly sweating will mean I’ll be replacing them regularly. So I was excited to check out Outdoor Tech’s Orcas, both because they are wireless and because they fit inside the ear. Less sweat all over everything, yay!

Unfortunately, the Orcas were horribly uncomfortable for me. I have small ears, so even the smallest ear tips (there are 3 sizes) were too big. It hurt to have them in for even 5 minutes. I tried them out while doing something that didn’t involve a lot of movement — weeding — and even then they kept falling out of my ears. I had to keep taking my gloves off and forcing them back in my ears. So I can’t imagine how they would stay in for anything more active. The “ear fins” are a neat idea, but again, both pairs are too big for me. I squished them in, but one shake of my head dislodged them.

Another note for the ear fins — if you have any piercings inside your ears, such as a rook or a forward helix, they won’t fit.

I did have trouble pairing the earbuds with my phone, but after tweeting to Outdoor Tech, they set me up with tech support and I had a reply within 10 minutes. (Email is support@outdoortech.com).

The sound quality was okay, nothing super great.

My main issue with the earbuds is just that they’re so uncomfortable! If you have small ears or problems wearing this type of headphones, I’d skip them. I’ll be sticking to my Skullcandys.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black)

Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount This TV makes me feel bad for ever having given another product 5 stars. It is really just about perfect. Instead of wasting a lot of space talking about the quality of the picture (believe me, it is there), I am going to concentrate on some finer points, particularly those real and perceived weak points:

(This is replacing a 2009 Sony Z-Series TV, which I also love and still consider a fantastic TV; it was the first year of Internet-capable TVs if I remember correctly, and I used the DLNA features with Universal Media Server, but could never get a Plex profile to work right, so I am happy to have a newer TV that supports Plex via App, besides for the 4k, HDR, etc., etc. I have a bunch of other TVs scattered about, but the other two I use most are less expensive Samsung Smart models from five or so years ago.)

Back to (possible) negatives:

I wasn't sure I would like the stand and style. I always hated those Samsung TVs with the plastic grey legs, and I thought this would look too much like that. I thought my ideal stand was either a perfect 90-degree version of the Sony A1E, or perhaps the A8F, which I had my eye on due to its very low profile, minimalist stand. Anyway, this one looks so much better in real life than I expected. It's actually metal, and fairly dark. Placed on low furniture, it looks great walking by, and sits at the right height while watching. I guess it is made to fit a Sony sound bar perfectly (I use full surround setup, so I don't care). But I am much, much happier with the looks than I thought I would be. If that is your hesitation, go check it out in a store (before coming back for the right price).

Thickness: its thicker than some, including last year's 930E, but the way it angles out from the back gives a much sleeker appearance than you may expect just from looking at the dimensions. You only see its thickness at about 80 degrees to the side. Overall, it sits back far and takes up little extra room than it has to. The TV looks as great off as it does on.

I read a professional review that mentioned the picture doesn't look as good from a side angle. I guess that's true, but it's not nearly as drastic of a change as it sounded from the review. In fact, one of the best TV seats in my house is about 30-degrees off-center, and I don't see a difference from there at all. At 45-degrees, you start to see a difference.

Above mentioned professional review also mentioned the Android TV thing can be a little clunky. I don't feel it, to be honest. It's been nothing but good surprises for me. One thing that could be improved is customization of your home screen. You can re-order some apps, but I haven't figured out how to delete the shortcuts for stuff that isn't even downloaded. And I'm never going to play goofy games on my TV (besides real video games), so how can I get rid of that whole section that is taking up space. You can block recommended content, so after them pushing some crapware on you initially, you can basically run add-free. Looks like you'll probably have to sign in to Google, though, but you can make a new account just for your TV (which is what I do for every device).

The downward facing ports look really good with the cable management, so good that I really don't want to use any of the side inputs for permanent setups. For that reason, they should have put the IR blaster and composite input facing down as well (not that I need them, as I don't have cable, but some people will).

Not that I even checked my link speed, but manual says Ethernet port is 100mbps. Can't imagine you'll ever need more than that unless you expect to run uncompressed video without a converter.

The remote is nicer than I expected, but still not as nice as my old one. Plus, although it has Bravia Sync, it doesn't easily just control my stereo the way I would like it to (as my old Sony TV did).Not sure why there has to be a Google button on the remote. Or even Netflix. These should be programmable. Actually, four programmable Apps and/or Input buttons would be greatly appreciated in their place.

That's about it for nitpicking. Here's some things that are totally awesome (besides all the obvious):

It can read all commonly used containers for video files, including *mkv, and it can decompress 4k HEVC (H.265) video natively. So even though my NAS cannot transcode 4k on the fly, if I set it to run at full quality, the TV does it just fine! And since H.265 was made because of 4k video, here's hoping we don't have formats this TV can't play any time soon. This is just fantastic to me, as I really love my NAS' Plex server function. You can also play up to 4k H.265 video right off a hard drive via USB.

My UMS media server is showing up under Video devices (which is where the DLNA servers show up), but you can't see the files. I haven't messed with it much (because now I don't care), but I assume they'll get a profile working before long.

I love the built-in TV guide function and also the way you can browse other channels along the bottom of your screen without changing the channel. These are both great features (the TV guide function on my old TV was abandoned after a few years, but I expect this one will continue to operate). I do not have or want cable, so now I have the features that are nice to have with cable without the burden of slow response cable boxes and the burden of dealing with Comcast.

I haven't even tried out the professional settings (or even messed with anything but motionflow) because the TV is impressing me every second it's on. Again, as this is the first 4k TV to reside in my house, I guess I should be amazed. But the blacks as bars on movies wider than 16:9 are so black you don't notice them. Space scenes are to die for. 4k is done right here: this is the high end of quality, about the only thing worth removing my old Z-series for. I just love it. It looks amazing on and off, and does everything I want it to do (mainly Plex, and Netflix is nice now and then as well). I'm so happy that Plex works so well with this TV without an expensive NAS upgrade, even with movies encoded at 2160p and 7.1 surround. Just fantastic.

It's better than I expected even from Sony's almost-second-to-flagship model. About as high end as they come before they jump up drastically in price. I wouldn't have anything less on my primary TV stand, and I don't need anything more. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount

CON: Personal pet peeve. The only con is on 60 inch TVs you cannot reach behind easily to use the security brackets.You have to use an 18 inch long screw driver or similar size to tighten them. (booklet does not say this . Only says use a screwdriver)They are not needed because the weight of the TV holds in in place. In my opinion, I like to do everything by the instructions. Not tighten the security brackets made me feel like I skipped a step. I will say its stays in place, and does not move, jiggle etc. Lifting the bottom of a 60 inch is not easy, so there is no worry about it being easily done, even by a kid since the hooks are on the top. Other reviewers have said security brackets are not needed to hold it in place. I just left them barely connected so I could have the option to screw on later.

ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear TL;DR— not worth the extra cost, it will break and the lifetime warranty is a scam (website doesn’t work, always out of stock), just order a cheaper one and replace— IF you can somehow get Zagg to honor the warranty they will charge you at least $7 to send you a new one when this breaks (and it will def. break)

This was a great screen protector for the several months it lasted before cracking. That partially justifies the steep price tag compared to other screen protectors— but not really.

After I purchased this from amazon I registered this product on the Zagg website, which is necessary to potentially claim a replacement through the “lifetime” warranty program. When it broke, I logged back into their website to order a replacement. The first thing that was annoying was they had a message saying any product ordered within a several years long period would need to be re-registered after they had redesigned their website— my screen protector did not fall into this category, but I assume many people were out of luck on their warranties since they probably no longer had their receipts from screen protectors they had already registered. There was no email or anything warning consumers of this issue, although it’s possible it went out to only the affected people.

When I tried to order a replacement for my broken screen protector I got an error message telling me to try again later. Then the screen protector was out of stock. Then the website is down for maintenance. Then it was out of stock again. The Zagg screen protector on my phone is also broken and also had a warranty. Between the two I have been unable to order a replacement despite trying many, many times. I‘m not a computer engineer or anything, but my computer literacy is usually sufficient to navigate consumer websites. I’m pretty sure the issue is not with me, and if I am doing something wrong it’s because they have intentionally made their website impossible to navigate.

Eventually I gave up and just replaced the screen protector on my phone with a cheaper one. I was able to buy 2 new screen protectors for the same price as the SHIPPING for what the warranty replacement for the Zagg screen protector would have been if it was ever in stock when their website was working, and the difference in quality is negligible.

I don’t appreciate paying extra for a warranty that is not honored and having my time wasted trying to order a replacement when it’s clearly designed to be impossible. I also ended up keeping a broken screen protector on my phone and iPad for months while trying over and over again to order my replacement since it was under warranty.

Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras 48 LED unit - (since several items are listed under one product ID)
Positives:
- It is what it looks like, does what it claims to do, and basically works
- cheap
- comes with an AC adapter!! Wow. You can pay a lot for a light that doesn't

Negatives: I'm using this for Macro work (I'm new to macro) so that's the perspective I'm coming from
- Not Bright Enough! It's just not all that bright. Not enough to light a subject by itself for macro purposes. I doubt it's adequate for more than a highlight for portraiture. This is why 2 stars. If a light doesn't light - it's not a light.

Really that's it. This is not a knock to the light (and not why I gave it a low rating), but if you are planning on using it for macro, buy a flash instead. A flash will not only have higher output, but will help freeze the camera shake (a big macro problem). Also, I thought the full time light would be better for live insects (you can see what you're doing!), but it's the opposite. You need the flash to freeze action. Not a criticism (this light does not advertise itself as a flash), but something to know.

UPDATE: I used it a couple more times. I am finding it more useful than initially when very close in. I would still strongly recommend a flash for this unless you have a compelling reason for continuous illumination (e.g you're waiting for a bug to crawl into frame and it's too dark to see otherwise. Though the lights would probably scare the bug). If you have a pretty solid tripod setup, this can work for longer exposure macro. Not great though. Upped to 3 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
LensPen NLP-1C Lens Cleaner (Black with Gold Rings) This lens pen is just what I need in a compact, easy-to-carry product. I am a photographer who has to carry a lot of gear outside. Having something compact and light is essential.

One side is a brush to get rid of fine and large particles of material from the lens. The other side is to remove oils (e.g. fingerprints) and is made of a fine material that has a carbon dust cleaning solution embedded in it.

The first three to five uses can be a bit frustrating as this carbon dust is quite heavy and will actually leave a slight residue on the lens. In this case I just used the brush first, the carbon cleaner second, and then finished up with the brush again to remove any extra carbon. I had no artifacts in my photos at all. After the initial break-in period this lens pen performs flawlessly.

The pen is close to 4 inches long (without the brush extended) and about 3/4 inches wide. Its actually very compact and light. It has a tab on the cap to be able to secure it while its in a pocket, just like a regular pen. The brush is about an inch long and is used by extending it out of the end of the pen. It adds about an inch of length when extended. The carbon cleaner is covered by a cap which is screwed off in order to expose the cleaning surface. I wish there was a spot to put this cap while using the carbon cleaning side. Its the only long term con to this pen.

Pros:
*Light
*Compact
*Cleans lenses well
*Easy to carry in pocket
*Cheap

Cons:
*Carbon dust residue for first 3-5 uses.(-1/4 star)
*Cap has no place to be put on the pen while using it. (-1/4 star)

Overall 4.5/5 (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 star rating

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.
text_fidelity_b: LensPen NLP-1C Lens Cleaner (Black with Gold Rings)

Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black Like everyone in California, we've been having a lot of power outages and spotty power, and through that, I've been really made aware how important it is to have steady, continuous power to my devices and not be affected by brownouts or power surges. I also really appreciate that when the power goes out suddenly, I have enough time to save my work, print a document, or do any last critical wrap up before things go dark. This battery backup has been great!

If you have used battery backup in the past you generally know what to expect, you plug it into the wall, plug in your devices, and when the power goes out you have a little bit of time, depending on which devices are sapping power from it and how much juice they take, to finish up what you are doing and shut down properly.

What is interesting to me about this one is that it has something that automatically powers down accessory devices like your monitor or scanner when the master device is off. So I have the one plug for the master device, which is my computer, and one plug that is on battery backup that will power down and accessory device like my monitor when my computer is not on, and three plugs that will power down accessory devices and not have them on battery backup, good for things like my scanner. While I haven't hooked up a power reader to determine exactly my savings, I do know for sure that some of these accessory devices are indeed using power when they are not being used, so I really appreciate the thoughtfulness of this.

There are also some regular plugs, some of which are battery backup and some not. This is perfect because there are ample plugs for everything and I can really set things up just the way I need so that my printer is not drawing battery power during a power outage unless I actually want it to.

It's working as expected and seems to be designed with care. I definitely recommend this.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Canon PowerShot SD1100IS 8MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Blue) (OLD MODEL) This is a solid little camera that can provide excellent image quality under the right conditions. But it has two glaring deficiencies:

1. No fill flash option in auto mode. (There is a fill flash option in manual mode, but it's not easy for the casual user to find.) There's red-eye reduction, of course, and you can turn the flash off completely or let the camera decide when to fire it. But with the camera in auto mode, you can't tell it to fire the flash on every shot, regardless of what its sensor thinks. Major bummer when you want to photograph a backlit subject.

2. Shot-to-shot time is agonizingly slow, and focus time isn't especially speedy, either. This is a problem when, for example, you want to catch quick snaps of the animals you see on Disney World's Kilimanjaro Safaris. Ask me how I know.

I'm sure this is a fine camera for people who want to photograph landscapes, still lifes, and posed portraits. For candid shots of subjects in motion, it's not so great.
text_fidelity_b: Canon PowerShot SD1100IS 8MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Blue) (OLD MODEL)

The picture is crystal clear and it's really easy to use. The voice search works extremely well. There are tons of free shows to watch, and free good music as well that you can play on your other devices free of charge. I will gladly renew my Prime subscription, even if I do have to pay for a movie once in a while. Also note, jaded Directv users- Amazon charges much less to watch a new movie. text_fidelity_a:
Logitech M500 Corded Mouse – Wired USB Mouse for Computers and Laptops, with Hyper-Fast Scrolling, Dark Gray When my trusty Microsoft Intellimouse died, I had a hard time finding a replacement. I wanted to stay with a corded mouse, and needed a minimum of five buttons. I also wanted the ability to scroll horizontially, a feature not on the Intellimouse that I had. Not many to choose from.

But, found the M500 and gave it a shot. Very pleased with it. The overall ergonomics are excellent - I have large hands, and most mice are too small for comfort. This fits perfectly.

The button placement is excellent, although I wish the page up and page down buttons were a wee bit larger. The best feature is the free-wheeling scroll wheel. You can unlock it so it spins freely and cruse through many pages with just a single spin. It also can be used as a conventional scroll wheel when the lock button is re-engaged.

The software allows you to re-map pretty much any of the keys to do what you want them to do. My mouse did not have the CD - had to download the software from the Logitech site. Without the software you only have basic functionality. Zero problems loading and running it on XP with SP3.

Very pleased, and highly recommend.

UPDATE Sept 2018: After many years of use, my M500 started to fail. The mouse tracking worked fine, as did all the buttons. However, the scroll wheel would not work well most of the time. I expect it's due to getting gunked up over the years. Took a look at the options out there and the M500 is still the best choice for my needs, so I got another one. Still very pleased with the performance and features.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M500 Corded Mouse – Wired USB Mouse for Computers and Laptops, with Hyper-Fast Scrolling, Dark Gray

I used this for my 42" Olevia LCD. I used the shortest screws of the proper thread size and pitch and also added own 1/4" Washer so the screws would not bottom out on the TV inserts. It would be nice if they added another hole for each side for an additional lag).

The price was fantastic. No box store could touch this price, nor adjust ability. I put this on the wall the day it arrived (Tuesday Aug 30th), so not even a week yet, so time will tell how it holds up.

Also, I did not get this very adjustable mount for constant or even occasional moving. We placed the TV in the corner of the room very high off the floor and a standard mount would not have allowed for this positioning.

The documentation was not the best, but was sufficient.

ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This is a very easy to use timer with some features that I’ve not come across before. It offers three main modes:

1) Clock – standard digital clock
2) Count up timer – can count up from zero to time events. It counts in whole seconds, so it’s not a true stopwatch.
3) Count down timer - you can set it to count down to zero.

The three modes are set by a sliding switch on the left so it’s very easy to change between the modes. It also has a memory feature so you can store a value and re-use it. For example, I use the count down feature to time tea brews, and have set a value of 3 min into memory. To repeat the countdown all I have to do is press the memory button and it sets itself to 3 min.

The best feature is that you can turn off the beep! There are three notification methods: a standard beep, vibrate or a flashing red LED. That’s a huge plus since I usually carry the timer with me and find the beep to be very annoying. The light or vibrate options are far nicer to use. I would imagine the flashing LED light option would be especially appreciated by the hearing impaired. You set the notification type with a switch on the back.

The overall build quality feels very solid. The numbers are large (about 0.75 inches tall) and easy to read even though the screen is not backlit. There a clip on the back that includes a magnet, so you can position this on a fridge or stove hood. The clip does not detach, but the profile is low enough that it doesn’t cause a problem if you want to carry the timer in your pocket.

It runs on 1 AAA battery (included). The package is easy to open – no clamshell to have to wrestle with.

It’s a well-made timer with some great convenience features built in. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Fire TV Stick 4K, brilliant 4K streaming quality, TV and smart home controls, free and live TV I’ve had a few Fire TV sticks over the years, and generally I love them. For this model, the first one I got was a dud. It died in 2 days. Amazon took me through some reasonable troubleshooting steps, then replaced it quickly and easily. The second one is a lot better.

In general, I find the remote has a weird tendency to, I guess “rot” is the word. The case starts to feel like it’s covered in a sticky mess. I don’t know why. I guess that’s why the remote covers are so popular. Not a stopping point – they still work – just a point of note. The optional game controllers do not have this issue.

There are ample streaming options. I’ve yet to look for something, even less common things like Wonderium and Funimation, and not find it. The UI is easy to navigate. The device is responsive. I put it through a 7.1 sound system and it can handle that no problem.

A few things to note, not exactly faults of the product, but faults you will encounter while using the product.

For the Disney+ login, the trick of using the phone just errors out and asks to re-authenticate over and over. If you use a strong password, that can be a pain. Once it works, it’s fine, just a pain to set up.

For the Ubisoft+ integration, for many of the games it starts to load then fails. I don’t see the same issue on the same games on PC, so it’s probably related to the app. This was the primary purpose for which I bought the device, so it is a bit of a disappointment. Also note, you need the Luna service for this, which is totally worth it on its own, by the way. Also, at least for me, while the video streaming was fine over WiFi, the gaming required the Ethernet adapter.

It’s not perfect, but it’s outstanding for such a low price. I often use it rather than power up my PS5 to watch Netflix because it is so much more convenient, and of identical quality.
text_fidelity_b: Fire TV Stick 4K, brilliant 4K streaming quality, TV and smart home controls, free and live TV

Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black) I've been using a Linksys router for years and it never missed a beat (their wireless G model with the two antennas). But, after upgrading my Internet from DSL to cable, I thought a new router would be in order.

Before buying one I searched for reviews from computer and tech magazines/sites. Talk about confusing! I'd read one review that gave a sterling endorsement for a particular router; then another review from another site that gave the same router a horrible review.

Since my router needs are pretty basic (just use it to share Internet access) I concentrated on ease of install issues. In that regard there was consensus about how easy Linksys is to install. So I went with them again, and selected the 1200 model since it gave me all that I wanted/needed at a good price (but, to hedge my bets, I got it at a warehouse club so I could return it easily).

So happy with this router! Installation was SO simple -- if you can plug in a cable you can install this router. But, should you want to tinker with settings, you can also access the full, detailed configuration menu and tweak settings to your heart's content. I think it took me longer to open up the box and unwrap the router and power cord than it took to actually get it to work.

Performance so far has been excellent. I put it on the ground level of my house and have no problems getting a strong signal in the basement and upper level. I did find that it helps to put the router in the middle of the house rather than against a wall for best signal strength throughout the house.

Considering that my Linksys G is still cranking along after several years, I'm reasonably confident (or at least hopeful) that this will last me an equal length of time.

If you're looking for a solid, easy to install single band router, this is it. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Linksys N300: Wi-Fi Wireless Router, Linksys Connect, Parental Controls, Home Internet, Wireless Devices up to 300 Mbps Transfer Speed (Black)

Philips SPP4105B/17 10-Outlet Home Office Surge Protector (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The outlets are spaced so that the larger plugs don't block multiple slots. There is plenty of room, even for the large ones.

Rather than trickling out power to devices that aren't on, the system automatically shuts down power to the energy saving outlet when the main outlet is shut off. This is great if the energy savers are peripherals and the main is a PC, but if you're doing something other than a computer setup it can be a pain to remember to only plug an "always on" device into this slot. If you shut that device off, everything in the 7 energy saving outlets will lose power. The power loss will trigger if you reboot your machine, which means that all of your peripherals will go through a full boot cycle as well.

I'd have preferred a switch to enable or disable this feature, and an outlet for charging USB devices rather than coax.

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC3200 Wireless Wi-Fi Tri-Band Gigabit Router (Archer C3200) The router is amazing... Great speeds and looks visually appealing in a room. It has enough processing power that it is able to route data to many wired and wireless device simultaneously and not have any slow downs and the 6 flip out antennas allow the device to have plenty of range to reach even the far corners of the house.

The 3 bands of wireless signal are great, it consists of 1, 2.4ghz network, and 2, 5ghz networks, so that you can assign wireless traffic it's own separate band in order to prevent congestion of a single band.
Remember that a 2.4ghz band will reach further but will be slower, while a 5ghz band will be significantly faster while not reaching as far.

For the more advanced people out there, there are plenty of options that you would expect from a mid range router like this, custom DNS servers, MAC address blocking, port forwarding, DHCP fine tuning, and it also allows you to plug in a USB flash drive into the USB port to use as a small NAS.

The user interface is also quite nice, it is visually appealing and very modern, while retaining functionality and still having the advanced features available for the people who need it.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC3200 Wireless Wi-Fi Tri-Band Gigabit Router (Archer C3200)

Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
MOS Magnetic Cable Organizer- Black I’ve got a few devices now, as probably every body reading this. A smartphone, a tablet, and a cordless mouse that plugs in to charge every week or two. And a couple U.S.B. cords hanging around is a mess. First to find one when needed. Then where to stash it after the use. This little gizmo is the best.
When I first saw it, I’m thinking. Why didn’t I do something like this. And even now, since I have already seen the idea. I could make something like this out of stuff I have around this room. But it’s not expensive. So I want to try and see if they did ‘good’ work. Well, they did.
I really wondered how, a magnetic mount like this could be safe around computers. I thought that the magnetic force might be so pathetically small, as to render such a device useless. But, the little triangle thing, that is the home base for your cable collection; is also magnetized. So a small magnet on the cord, along with the magnetic flux of the mounting surface, makes for a ‘good’ grip. For cables, such as designed for, is perfect. I wanted to put a set of headphones up on this rack. But it never happened. Sure, they would stick, and hold. But then, when other cables would be attached, and detached, the headphones would fall. But cords, are a rock solid stick.
And it is pretty. I’m no designer, but I think it makes my desk look like I care. And it’s a conversation piece. I really like this piece. But I still think, I should have thought of this.
text_fidelity_b: MOS Magnetic Cable Organizer- Black

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black) There’s some good points to this bag, but there are also a number of limitations that keep it at a three star rating.

On the plus side, the build quality is, in usual Case Logic fashion, well done. Strong, even stitching throughout; nice straps and buckles; good quality zippers with easy to find pull tabs. It feels and looks quite nice.

Unfortunately, the overall design does not meet as high of a standard. The padding is thin throughout. While I know this is for lighter, smaller DSLRs, I did not feel it provided much security for my Canon Rebel XT with just a couple of lens (50mm and 85mm). It’s not a size issue – just to see if I could, I was able to fit in my Canon 5D Mark II with the Canon 70-200L zoom plus the hood. It’s not a size issue, but rather a padding issue. The foam is thin and is not nearly as dense and bump absorbing as packs from Tenba, Lowepro or Crumpler. Granted, this is addressing a lower price point, but it’s not that low. Other lower-end bags I’ve tried have far more robust padding.

The slot for the tablet is another issue. Great idea; poor execution. There is very little padding for the tablet – forget about putting in a tablet unless it has a hard case, since this backpack won’t offer much protection. Same for the side pockets which have no padding.

This is a good choice if you’re looking to tote very little gear and are willing to bring along the cases for the camera and lenses to aid in keeping them protected. This is not a good choice if you’re looking for a “grab and go” type of backpack. Nice looking, but poor protection.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic TBC-411 DSLR Compact Backpack (Black)

Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd) Updated-11/28/12 I thought charging problems were related to problems with my Kindle e-reader charger. I purchased the power charger and things seem to be better. However, when I plug it in to charge, it does not always start charging and I have to unplug it, wait, etc. And now I noticed that it isn't holding the charge very well. I called Amazon and they are sending me out a replacement right away. If the replacement doesn't have any issues, I will keep the 5 stars and assume i got one with a glitch. It happens. If there are still issues, then it will be an overall problem and my ratings will drop. There was a person on the forum page that also had this problem. Most others are reporting no issues with the battery. So for now, I will gave Amazon the benefit of the doubt.

I have only had this for a day so I have not explored everything. This is my first tablet so I have little to compare it to, but I have a Kindle e-reader which I love. I found this to be pretty user friendly considering I don't even have a smartphone so apps and touchscreens are new to me. I found the user's guide to me helpful as well as the Kindle forum to answer questions I didn't feel like looking for answers to. I had no problem uploading my favorite sites. Some said they couldn't watch movies but I have been able to with both Netflix and Amazon on demand.Also, I guess there were some issues with the sound in the first generation Fire. I didn't have any problems, I didn't even need to use full volume when watching shows.
I downloaded a few free apps to play around with. And of course my books. I like that I can download some to the Fire but if there is one I want to read that I already own, I can download it from kindle Cloud. I can read books without downloading them via the Cloud but that means keeping the wireless on. Same with music.
I'm not to great with touchscreens and I loathe fingerprints so I prefer to use the stylus that I got separately. I didn't get a charger (it comes with USB cord only but charging through the computer won't really work), the one for my Kindle fits but doesn't charge as fast. So I ended up ordering the fast charger as the Fire isn't meant to last as many hours as the Kindle e-reader. But I still think the battery life is pretty good.
I like reading on this, I thought the back-light would bother me, but I can adjust the brightness. I actually prefer reading in the portrait mode as it shows two pages and looks like a book page would.
So far I am very happy with this, my third Kindle device. I like Amazon and find them to be very user friendly when I need help so I have no concerns so far. If there are any issues, I will update my review because I take spending my money very seriously.

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirTag 4 Pack Honestly I was hesitant at buying these, having used Tiles in the past (disappointed). But these were lower in price than usual, so I bought some. IMPORTANT, you need at least one Apple device to set them up and use.
Short review: Awesome. Just buy them.
Longer review: Got them quickly and opens package and set up four of them. Took less than two/three minutes each. Pair with Apple device, (You can go in and personalize name, icon and a few others settings which takes few more minutes, but not hard or time consuming.)
I did two with an iPhone and two with an iPad. (I will try with my iMac when I add more).
I bought a bag of keyrings, I think twenty, of different colors, an a set of four wallet inserts. Love the keyrings, It takes some finagling, to get them in, not awful, just requires patience. Which I attached a set of keys to. Does not add a lot weight wise, and is noticable visually, and of course takes up some space, but nothing horrible.
The wallet inserts, is, ok. The size of a credit card, and is tapered across the wide side, going from one credit card thickness to twothree thick. There is a hole you put your Airtag and put it in your wallet. Just putting the Airtag your wallet makes big bump. Push come to shove it would work, but...
The wallet inserts adds some thickness to your wallet for sure, for me, not too awful. Not heavy, a bit heavier than a credit card. It works, but I am on the lookout for a better solution. I hear they have wallets made just for the Airtags, unless I can actually try one out, not ready for that debacle, or expense yet. (Anyone have tried one?).
These have come in handy already, someone grabbed the wrong keys and we were able to track them down a few towns over, honest mistake, we had theirs, they had ours. Misplaced wallet (fell out of workout pants) slid under car seat. Used play sound and tracking app, and found it pronto.
Plus numerous times set down in house, slid between cushions, fell into reusable shopping bags, someone picked up and moved them elsewhere in the house. Play sound, and or tracking app removes the stress and wasted time searching.
Getting ready for a long trip so I plan on dropping one in each suitcase and backpack.
It can be set to beep if it gets too far from your iDevice. Now this works best if you have an iPhone (or you never put your iPad down). So if at a restaurant, you set your keys down and walk away, you get so many feet, and it starts beeping.
There are a bunch of other accessories for the Airtag. A sticky sleeve, for say a laptop or tablet.
A friend even put one on her dogs, a new one likes to run away when she can ( yes they are working on training her, but in the meantime...).
If like me, you are a little flakey, and forgetful, these are awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirTag 4 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer** There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

Avantree Oasis B Bluetooth 5.0 Transmitter Receiver for TV, Home Stereo Speakers, Bypass Mode, Class 1 Long Range, LED Indicator, Optical AUX RCA, aptX Low Latency Audio Adapter for 2 Headphones I had previously owned another Bluetooth transmitter by Avantree, which cost very little less than this one, but the caliber of this transmitter is massively better than the old one. So they must have made some useful advances in the relevant technology in the four years since I last purchased a transmitter from them.

I have tested this transmitter with multiple Bluetooth headphones that I own, and in each case, the Bluetooth connects seamlessly. I like the fact that the transmitter speaks and lets me know when the Bluetooth has connected. And a split second after that, the sound from my TV comes through my Bluetooth headphones. My old Avantree transmitter had neither of those abilities. It would take up to 2 minutes to get it connected to my Bluetooth headphones after multiple tries, and the sound's clarity and volume weren't nearly as good.

As was the case with my previous transmitter, this one can handle multiple Bluetooth headphones at the same time. So far I have only attempted transmission with two at a time.

Finally, the appearance of this transmitter is much fancier than the old one. I will admit that it is about three times larger than the old one, but that is not really a problem for me, because the old one was tiny and this one is still conveniently small. It has some cute, space-age looking little antennas on it that the other one didn't have, which may partially account for why it works so much better.

All in all, I am very pleased with this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Avantree Oasis B Bluetooth 5.0 Transmitter Receiver for TV, Home Stereo Speakers, Bypass Mode, Class 1 Long Range, LED Indicator, Optical AUX RCA, aptX Low Latency Audio Adapter for 2 Headphones
